    assert circle_weight(17) != circle_weight(41)
    print("  -> W(17) = -2 but W(41) = -10: no function of p mod 8 can do this.")

    print("\nPrimes congruent to 1 mod 4:")
    for p in [13, 17]:
        print(f"    p = {p:>4}   p mod 4 = {p % 4}   W(p) = {circle_weight(p):>4}")
    assert circle_weight(13) != circle_weight(17)
    print("  -> the mod-4 dial dies too.")

    print("\nComposite moduli congruent to 5 mod 8:")
    for n in [21, 85, 205, 221]:
        print(f"    N = {n:>5}   N mod 8 = {n % 8}   W(N) = {circle_weight(n):>5}")
    assert circle_weight(21) != circle_weight(85)
    print("  -> W(21) = 0 but W(85) = -4: the dial is broken at composite level too.")

    print("\nBUT the value mod 8 *is* a dial (the residual public part):")
    for p in [17, 41, 73, 89, 5, 13, 29, 37]:
        print(f"    p mod 8 = {p % 8}  =>  W(p) mod 8 = {circle_weight(p) % 8}")


def demo_blindness() -> None:
    banner("Blind families and collisions")
    print("W(3q) = 0 for every prime q != 3 -- an infinite zero-information family:")
    for q in [5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23]:
        w = circle_weight(3 * q)
        print(f"    N = 3 * {q:>3} = {3*q:>4}   W(N) = {w}")
        assert w == 0
    print("\nCollisions: W(15) = W(21) = 0, so W cannot determine a factorisation.")


def demo_weil_floor_attainment() -> None:
    banner("Near-attainment of the Weil bound  |W(p)| <= 2 sqrt(p)")
    print(f"{'p':>6} {'W(p)':>7} {'2 sqrt(p)':>11} {'ratio W^2/(4p)':>16}")
    best: List[Tuple[float, int, int]] = []
    for p in primes_up_to(500):
        if p % 4 != 1:
            continue
        w = circle_weight(p)
        best.append((w * w / (4 * p), p, w))
    best.sort(reverse=True)
    for ratio, p, w in best[:8]:
        print(f"{p:>6} {w:>7} {2*math.sqrt(p):>11.3f} {ratio:>16.4f}")
    print("\nThe bound is sharp: no constant c < 3.9 works in W(p)^2 <= c p.")


def demo_decorrelation(trials: int = 2000, seed: int = 20260813) -> None:
    banner("10. Factor-dependent but unstructured: permutation test on 40 semiprimes")
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    good = [p for p in primes_up_to(400) if p % 4 == 1 and p > 3]
    cache: Dict[int, int] = {p: circle_weight(p) for p in good}

    pairs: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    seen = set()
    while len(pairs) < 40:
        p, q = sorted(rng.sample(good, 2))
        if (p, q) not in seen:
            seen.add((p, q))
            pairs.append((p, q))

    w_values = [cache[p] * cache[q] for p, q in pairs]
    covariates: Dict[str, Callable[[Tuple[int, int]], float]] = {
        "p (smaller factor)": lambda pq: float(pq[0]),
        "q (larger factor)": lambda pq: float(pq[1]),
        "p + q": lambda pq: float(pq[0] + pq[1]),
        "|p - q|": lambda pq: float(abs(pq[0] - pq[1])),
    }

    print(f"{'covariate':>20} {'|corr|':>9} {'null 95%':>10}   verdict")
    for name, fn in covariates.items():
        cov = [fn(pq) for pq in pairs]
        obs = abs(pearson(w_values, cov))
        thr = permutation_threshold(w_values, cov, trials, seed)
        verdict = "inside null (no signal)" if obs < thr else "EXCEEDS NULL"
        print(f"{name:>20} {obs:>9.3f} {thr:>10.3f}   {verdict}")

    print("\nAlso check the semiprime Weil floor |W(N)| <= 4 sqrt(N) on the sample:")
    worst = max((abs(w) / (4 * math.sqrt(p * q)), p, q, w)
                for (p, q), w in zip(pairs, w_values))
    ratio, p, q, w = worst
    print(f"    tightest case: N = {p} * {q} = {p*q}, W(N) = {w}, "
          f"|W(N)|/(4 sqrt N) = {ratio:.4f}")
    for (p, q), w in zip(pairs, w_values):
        assert w * w <= 16 * p * q


def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    demo_collapse_identity()
    demo_multiplicativity()
    demo_vanishing_and_parity()
    demo_second_moment_and_weil()
    demo_jacobsthal_and_two_squares()
    demo_not_a_residue_dial()
    demo_blindness()
    demo_weil_floor_attainment()
    demo_decorrelation()
    banner("All assertions passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

demos.name: Semiprime Census: Information-Theoretic Collapse of the Witness
demos.description: A brute-force census over all semiprimes N = pq below a cutoff that quantifies exactly how much the statistic could possibly say. It reports how many semiprimes are annihilated outright (about 79% below 20000, those with a prime factor congruent to 3 mod 4), how many distinct values the statistic takes against how many factorisations exist, the resulting average collision multiplicity (about six factorisations per value even after restricting to the informative quarter), the worst individual collisions, the tightest observed approach to the semiprime Weil ceiling |W(N)| <= 4 sqrt(N), and a heuristic bit count showing the channel carries roughly 6 bits where 11 bits of factorisation live.
demos.code:
"""
Semiprime census: how much can the Jacobi-signed circle count possibly say?

This demo quantifies the failure of W(N) = sum over the circle x^2 + y^2 = 1 of
the Jacobi symbol (x/N) as a factoring witness, by brute-force census over all
semiprimes N = p q (p < q, both odd) below a cutoff:

  * how many are annihilated outright (some factor = 3 mod 4);
  * how many distinct values W takes, versus how many factorisations there are;
  * the resulting average collision multiplicity -- the number of different
    factorisations sharing a value, which is a lower bound on the ambiguity any
    W-based attack must resolve;
  * the largest observed |W(N)| / (4 sqrt N), confirming the semiprime Weil floor.

Self-contained: standard library only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter
from math import sqrt
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = [True] * limit
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def circle_weight_prime(p: int) -> int:
    return sum(legendre(x * (1 - x * x) % p, p) for x in range(p))


def census(cutoff: int = 20000, prime_cap: int = 700) -> None:
    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(prime_cap) if p > 2]
    wtab: Dict[int, int] = {p: circle_weight_prime(p) for p in ps}

    records: List[Tuple[int, int, int, int]] = []
    for i, p in enumerate(ps):
        for q in ps[i + 1:]:
            n = p * q
            if n >= cutoff:
                break
            records.append((n, p, q, wtab[p] * wtab[q]))

    total = len(records)
    zeros = sum(1 for _, _, _, w in records if w == 0)
    values = Counter(w for _, _, _, w in records)
    distinct = len(values)
    nonzero_records = [r for r in records if r[3] != 0]

    print(f"semiprimes N = p q < {cutoff} with distinct odd factors : {total}")
    print(f"  annihilated (W(N) = 0, some factor = 3 mod 4)         : "
          f"{zeros}  ({100*zeros/total:.1f}%)")
    print(f"  distinct values of W over all of them                 : {distinct}")
    print(f"  average collision multiplicity                        : "
          f"{total/distinct:.1f} factorisations per value")

    if nonzero_records:
        nz_values = Counter(w for _, _, _, w in nonzero_records)
        print(f"  restricted to the informative quarter (W != 0)        : "
              f"{len(nonzero_records)} semiprimes, {len(nz_values)} values, "
              f"{len(nonzero_records)/len(nz_values):.1f} per value")

    print("\nworst collisions (same value, different factorisations):")
    for w, count in values.most_common(4):
        examples = [f"{p}*{q}" for _, p, q, ww in records if ww == w][:6]
        print(f"  W = {w:>6}  occurs {count:>4} times   e.g. " + ", ".join(examples))

    ratio, arg = max(((abs(w) / (4 * sqrt(n)), (n, p, q, w))
                      for n, p, q, w in records), default=(0.0, None))
    if arg:
        n, p, q, w = arg
        print(f"\ntightest Weil-floor case: N = {p}*{q} = {n}, W(N) = {w}, "
              f"|W|/(4 sqrt N) = {ratio:.4f}  (bound: <= 1)")

    print("\nBits of information, heuristically:")
    print(f"  log2(number of factorisations) = {__import__('math').log2(total):.1f} bits")
    print(f"  log2(number of W-values)       = {__import__('math').log2(distinct):.1f} bits")
    print("  -> the statistic cannot, even in principle, identify the factor pair.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    census()

algorithms.name: Linear-Time Evaluation of the Jacobi-Signed Circle Count via the Collapse Identity
algorithms.description: Evaluating the statistic straight from its geometric definition requires sweeping the whole torus (Z/NZ)^2 and testing each pair for membership on the circle: O(N^2 log N) bit operations. The collapse identity removes an entire dimension. Summing the y-coordinate away replaces the inner loop by the closed-form count chi(1-x^2)+1 of square roots, and the residual sum of the character over all x vanishes, leaving the one-dimensional cubic character sum W(N) = sum_x (x(1-x^2)/N). Each Jacobi symbol costs O(log N) by the reciprocity ladder (no factorisation of the modulus and no modular exponentiation required), so the total is O(N log N) bit operations and O(1) space. This is the fastest known evaluation of the statistic without knowing the factorisation of N, and it is precisely the cost barrier that disqualifies the statistic as a factoring witness: trial division already costs only O(sqrt N).
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT : odd modulus N >= 3
OUTPUT: W(N) = sum over the circle x^2+y^2=1 (mod N) of the Jacobi symbol (x/N)

function JACOBI(a, n):                       // O(log n)
    require n odd and n >= 1
    a <- a mod n ;  s <- +1
    while a != 0:
        while a is even:
            a <- a / 2
            if n mod 8 in {3, 5}: s <- -s     // supplementary law for 2
        swap(a, n)                            // quadratic reciprocity
        if a mod 4 = 3 and n mod 4 = 3: s <- -s
        a <- a mod n
    return s if n = 1 else 0                  // 0 iff gcd(a, N) > 1

function CIRCLE_WEIGHT(N):                   // O(N log N)
    total <- 0
    for x <- 0 to N-1:
        t <- x * (1 - x^2)  mod N             // the cubic -(x^3 - x)
        total <- total + JACOBI(t, N)
    return total

CORRECTNESS: for prime modulus, #{y : y^2 = a} = chi(a) + 1, so the inner sum over y
equals chi(x)(chi(1-x^2)+1); expanding gives the cubic sum plus sum_x chi(x) = 0.
For composite N both the circle and the Jacobi symbol split under the Chinese
Remainder Theorem, and the identity propagates multiplicatively.

algorithms.name: Second-Moment Certification of the Weil Floor over Quadratic Twists
algorithms.description: A certifying procedure that establishes, for a given prime p congruent to 1 mod 4, the entire chain of bounds and identities governing the statistic. It computes the full family of quadratic twist sums A(d) = sum_x chi(x^3 - dx) for all d, which costs O(p^2) character lookups after an O(p log p) precomputation of the Legendre table. From this family it certifies three facts. First the exact second moment sum_d A(d)^2 = 2p(p-1), a closed-form identity proved by expanding the square and evaluating an inner quadratic character sum. Second the Weil bound A(1)^2 <= 4p: since A(c^2 e) = chi(c)A(e), all p-1 nonzero square twists share the same squared value, and squaring being at most 2-to-1 forces (p-1)A(1)^2 <= 2 * 2p(p-1). Third the sharper Jacobsthal identity A(1)^2 + A(nu)^2 = 4p for any nonresidue nu, obtained by pushing the moment forward along the squaring map twice with complementary character weights. The output includes the two-square decomposition p = (A(1)/2)^2 + (A(nu)/2)^2 read directly off the twist sums, together with the observation that the whole family takes only three values up to sign: 0, plus or minus A(1), and plus or minus A(nu).
algorithms.code:
"""
Algorithm 2: second-moment certification of the Weil floor over quadratic twists.

For an odd prime p and d in Z/pZ set  A(d) = sum_x chi(x^3 - d x), the (negated)
trace of Frobenius of the quadratic twist y^2 = x^3 - dx.  The algorithm computes
all p twist sums, certifies the exact second moment

        sum_d A(d)^2 = 2 p (p - 1),

and derives from it, with no algebraic geometry, the Weil bound A(1)^2 <= 4p and
the sharper Jacobsthal identity A(1)^2 + A(nu)^2 = 4p for a nonresidue nu.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def all_twist_sums(p: int) -> List[int]:
    """A(d) for every d, computed in O(p^2) character evaluations."""
    chi = [legendre(a, p) for a in range(p)]
    cubes = [(x * x * x) % p for x in range(p)]
    out: List[int] = []
    for d in range(p):
        s = 0
        for x in range(p):
            s += chi[(cubes[x] - d * x) % p]
        out.append(s)
    return out


def first_nonresidue(p: int) -> int:
    for v in range(2, p):
        if legendre(v, p) == -1:
            return v
    raise ValueError("no nonresidue")


def certify(p: int) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Return a certificate bundle for the Weil floor at the prime p."""
    if p % 4 != 1:
        raise ValueError("the identity is stated for p = 1 (mod 4)")
    a = all_twist_sums(p)
    nu = first_nonresidue(p)
    moment = sum(v * v for v in a)
    return {
        "p": p,
        "W(p) = A(1)": a[1],
        "A(nu)": a[nu],
        "second moment": moment,
        "2p(p-1)": 2 * p * (p - 1),
        "moment identity holds": moment == 2 * p * (p - 1),
        "A(1)^2 + A(nu)^2": a[1] ** 2 + a[nu] ** 2,
        "4p": 4 * p,
        "Jacobsthal identity holds": a[1] ** 2 + a[nu] ** 2 == 4 * p,
        "Weil bound holds": a[1] ** 2 <= 4 * p,
        "fraction of ceiling": a[1] ** 2 / (4 * p),
        "distinct |A(d)| values": sorted({abs(v) for v in a}),
    }


def two_squares(p: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """p = a^2 + b^2 with a = W(p)/2 odd, read straight off the twist sums."""
    a = all_twist_sums(p)
    nu = first_nonresidue(p)
    return a[1] // 2, a[nu] // 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for p in (13, 17, 29, 41, 173):
        cert = certify(p)
        a, b = two_squares(p)
        print(f"p = {p}")
        for k, v in cert.items():
            print(f"    {k:>26} : {v}")
        print(f"    {'two squares':>26} : {p} = {a}^2 + {b}^2  (a odd: {a % 2 != 0})")

algorithms.name: Permutation-Null Test for Factor Leakage in a Multiplicative Statistic
algorithms.description: A distribution-free hypothesis test for the question that decides the fate of any candidate arithmetic witness: does the statistic carry recoverable information about the factor pair? Given a multiplicative statistic F with F(pq) = F(p)F(q), the procedure samples semiprimes from an admissible prime pool (here both factors congruent to 1 mod 4, since otherwise the statistic vanishes identically), evaluates F on the pool once and reuses it multiplicatively, and computes the Pearson correlation of F(N) against each of several simple functionals of the factor pair: the smaller factor, the larger factor, their sum, their absolute difference, and log N. Because sample correlations at n = 40 are noisy and the F-values are heavy-tailed, significance is assessed against a permutation null: the F-values are repeatedly reshuffled against the fixed covariate, which destroys any association while preserving both marginal distributions exactly, and the 95th percentile of the resulting |r| distribution is the decision threshold. Cost is O(S * P) to build the statistic table on a pool of primes below P plus O(T * S) for T permutations on a sample of size S. On the Jacobi-signed circle count every observed |r| falls well inside the null, confirming the statistic is factor-dependent but unstructured.
algorithms.code:
"""
Algorithm 3: permutation test for factor leakage in a multiplicative statistic.

Given a multiplicative statistic F with F(pq) = F(p) F(q), the question "does F
leak the factorisation?" is operationalised as: is F(N) correlated, across a
sample of semiprimes, with any simple functional of the factor pair -- p, q,
p + q, |p - q|?  Correlation alone is meaningless at small sample sizes, so the
observed |r| is compared with a permutation null obtained by reshuffling the
F-values against the fixed covariate, which destroys any association while
preserving both marginal distributions exactly.

Complexity: O(S * N_max) to build the statistic table (dominated by evaluating F
on the primes involved) plus O(T * S) for T permutations on a sample of size S.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def circle_weight_prime(p: int) -> int:
    """W(p) = sum_x chi(x(1 - x^2))."""
    return sum(legendre(x * (1 - x * x) % p, p) for x in range(p))


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = [True] * limit
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def pearson(xs: Sequence[float], ys: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    n = len(xs)
    mx, my = sum(xs) / n, sum(ys) / n
    sx = math.sqrt(sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs))
    sy = math.sqrt(sum((y - my) ** 2 for y in ys))
    return 0.0 if sx == 0 or sy == 0 else \
        sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / (sx * sy)


def permutation_test(
    values: Sequence[float],
    covariate: Sequence[float],
    trials: int = 2000,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Return (observed |r|, 95th percentile of null, empirical p-value)."""
    obs = abs(pearson(values, covariate))
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = list(values)
    nulls: List[float] = []
    for _ in range(trials):
        rng.shuffle(pool)
        nulls.append(abs(pearson(pool, covariate)))
    nulls.sort()
    pval = sum(1 for v in nulls if v >= obs) / trials
    return obs, nulls[int(0.95 * trials)], pval


def run(sample_size: int = 40, prime_cap: int = 400, seed: int = 20260813) -> None:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = [p for p in primes_up_to(prime_cap) if p % 4 == 1 and p > 3]
    table: Dict[int, int] = {p: circle_weight_prime(p) for p in pool}

    pairs: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    seen = set()
    while len(pairs) < sample_size:
        p, q = sorted(rng.sample(pool, 2))
        if (p, q) not in seen:
            seen.add((p, q))
            pairs.append((p, q))

    stat = [float(table[p] * table[q]) for p, q in pairs]
    covariates: Dict[str, Callable[[Tuple[int, int]], float]] = {
        "p": lambda pq: float(pq[0]),
        "q": lambda pq: float(pq[1]),
        "p + q": lambda pq: float(pq[0] + pq[1]),
        "|p - q|": lambda pq: float(abs(pq[0] - pq[1])),
        "log N": lambda pq: math.log(pq[0] * pq[1]),
    }

    print(f"{'covariate':>12} {'|r|':>8} {'null 95%':>10} {'p-value':>9}  verdict")
    for name, fn in covariates.items():
        cov = [fn(pq) for pq in pairs]
        obs, thr, pval = permutation_test(stat, cov, seed=seed)
        verdict = "no evidence of leakage" if obs < thr else "SIGNAL"
        print(f"{name:>12} {obs:>8.3f} {thr:>10.3f} {pval:>9.3f}  {verdict}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

visualizations.name: The Weil Band: Normalised Values and Their Distribution
visualizations.description: Two panels. The left plots W(p)/(2 sqrt p) for every prime p congruent to 1 mod 4 below the cutoff, against the shaded band [-1, 1] that the Weil bound forbids the statistic to leave; near-attainments within three percent of the ceiling are circled, showing the bound is not merely an order-of-magnitude estimate but is approached again and again. The right panel histograms the same normalised values against the semicircle density (2/pi) sqrt(1 - t^2), the Sato-Tate shape expected for the non-supersingular half of this CM family. Together they make the central negative point visible: the statistic fills its square-root window and never escapes it, so its total variation is O(sqrt N) against a search space of size N.
visualizations.code:
"""
Visualization: the Weil floor and the Sato-Tate-like spread of the normalised statistic.

Left panel  : W(p) / (2 sqrt p) for every prime p = 1 (mod 4) below the cutoff.
              The band [-1, 1] is the Weil ceiling; the points crowd it but never
              leave it, and near-attainments (ratio > 0.97) are highlighted.
Right panel : histogram of the same normalised values against the semicircle
              density (2/pi) sqrt(1 - t^2), the Sato-Tate law for a CM family
              restricted to its non-supersingular half.

Requires: matplotlib, numpy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = [True] * limit
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def circle_weight_prime(p: int) -> int:
    """W(p) = sum_x chi(x(1 - x^2))."""
    return sum(legendre(x * (1 - x * x) % p, p) for x in range(p))


def main(cutoff: int = 4000) -> None:
    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(cutoff) if p % 4 == 1]
    ws = [circle_weight_prime(p) for p in ps]
    ts = [w / (2.0 * math.sqrt(p)) for p, w in zip(ps, ws)]

    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2),
                                   gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.6, 1]})

    ax1.axhspan(-1, 1, color="#f6c453", alpha=0.10)
    ax1.axhline(1, color="#f6c453", lw=1.6, label=r"Weil ceiling $\pm 2\sqrt{p}$")
    ax1.axhline(-1, color="#f6c453", lw=1.6)
    ax1.axhline(0, color="#94a3b8", lw=0.6)

    near = [(p, t) for p, t in zip(ps, ts) if abs(t) > 0.97]
    ax1.scatter(ps, ts, s=13, color="#4fd1c5", alpha=0.75, label=r"$W(p)/(2\sqrt p)$")
    if near:
        ax1.scatter([p for p, _ in near], [t for _, t in near], s=48,
                    facecolors="none", edgecolors="#f78da7", lw=1.4,
                    label="within 3% of the ceiling")
    ax1.set_xlabel("prime $p \\equiv 1 \\pmod 4$")
    ax1.set_ylabel("normalised statistic")
    ax1.set_title("The statistic never escapes the square-root band")
    ax1.set_ylim(-1.25, 1.25)
    ax1.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=9)

    ax2.hist(ts, bins=24, range=(-1, 1), density=True, color="#7aa2f7",
             alpha=0.75, edgecolor="#0b0f16")
    grid = np.linspace(-1, 1, 400)
    ax2.plot(grid, (2 / math.pi) * np.sqrt(np.clip(1 - grid ** 2, 0, None)),
             color="#f6c453", lw=2, label=r"$\frac{2}{\pi}\sqrt{1-t^2}$")
    ax2.set_xlabel("normalised statistic")
    ax2.set_ylabel("density")
    ax2.set_title("Distribution inside the band")
    ax2.legend(fontsize=9)

    fig.suptitle("The Jacobi-signed circle count sits at the Weil floor", fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("weil_floor.png", dpi=150)
    print(f"{len(ps)} primes; max |normalised| = {max(abs(t) for t in ts):.4f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: The Two-Square Conservation Law Made Visible
visualizations.description: For each prime p congruent to 1 mod 4 the pair of residue and nonresidue twist sums satisfies exactly A(1)^2 + A(nu)^2 = 4p, so halving gives a lattice point (a, b) sitting precisely on the circle of radius sqrt(p), with the odd leg a = W(p)/2 delivered by the circle count itself. The left panel draws these circles and their lattice points, coloured by p mod 8; the right panel replots the same data in normalised coordinates, where every prime lands exactly on the unit quarter-circle. The second panel is the verdict in one image: a witness reading the horizontal coordinate is reading one projection of a point pinned to a circle, so a large signal in the readable leg is paid for exactly by a small one in the unreadable twin, with 4p conserved.
visualizations.code:
"""
Visualization: the two-square conservation law made visible.

For each prime p = 1 (mod 4) the pair (A(1), A(nu)) of residue and nonresidue
twist sums satisfies exactly A(1)^2 + A(nu)^2 = 4p, where A(1) = W(p) is the
Jacobi-signed circle count.  Halving, (a, b) = (W(p)/2, A(nu)/2) is a lattice
point on the circle of radius sqrt(p) -- i.e. a Gaussian-integer factorisation
p = a^2 + b^2 with the odd leg a delivered by the statistic.

The figure draws, for a family of primes, the circle of radius sqrt(p) and the
lattice point on it, coloured by p mod 8, and annotates the odd leg.  The visual
message: the statistic is one coordinate of a point pinned to a circle -- a
projection of a conserved quantity, which is precisely why it cannot leak the
factorisation of a semiprime.

Requires: matplotlib, numpy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def twist_sum(p: int, d: int) -> int:
    return sum(legendre((x * x * x - d * x) % p, p) for x in range(p))


def nonresidue(p: int) -> int:
    for v in range(2, p):
        if legendre(v, p) == -1:
            return v
    raise ValueError


def legs(p: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """(a, b) with p = a^2 + b^2, a = W(p)/2 odd."""
    return twist_sum(p, 1) // 2, twist_sum(p, nonresidue(p)) // 2


def main() -> None:
    ps: List[int] = [5, 13, 17, 29, 37, 41, 53, 61, 73, 89, 97, 101, 109, 113,
                     137, 149, 157, 173, 181, 193, 197, 229, 233, 241, 257, 269,
                     277, 281, 293]
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 6))

    theta = np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 400)
    for p in ps:
        a, b = legs(p)
        r = math.sqrt(p)
        colour = "#4fd1c5" if p % 8 == 1 else "#f78da7"
        ax1.plot(r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), color=colour, lw=0.6, alpha=0.45)
        ax1.scatter([a], [b], s=26, color=colour, zorder=3)
        if p in (5, 17, 41, 173, 293):
            ax1.annotate(f"$p={p}$", (a, b), textcoords="offset points",
                         xytext=(6, 5), fontsize=8, color="#e9eef8")
    ax1.axhline(0, color="#94a3b8", lw=0.5)
    ax1.axvline(0, color="#94a3b8", lw=0.5)
    ax1.set_aspect("equal")
    ax1.set_xlabel("$a = W(p)/2$  (odd leg)")
    ax1.set_ylabel(r"$b = A(\nu)/2$  (even leg)")
    ax1.set_title(r"Each prime pins a lattice point to its circle: $a^2+b^2=p$")
    ax1.scatter([], [], color="#4fd1c5", label="$p \\equiv 1 \\pmod 8$")
    ax1.scatter([], [], color="#f78da7", label="$p \\equiv 5 \\pmod 8$")
    ax1.legend(fontsize=9, loc="upper left")

    # the trade-off: |a| against |b|, normalised
    xs = []
    ys = []
    for p in ps:
        a, b = legs(p)
        xs.append(abs(a) / math.sqrt(p))
        ys.append(abs(b) / math.sqrt(p))
    ax2.scatter(xs, ys, s=34, color="#7aa2f7", zorder=3)
    t = np.linspace(0, math.pi / 2, 300)
    ax2.plot(np.cos(t), np.sin(t), color="#f6c453", lw=2,
             label="conservation law $|a|^2+|b|^2=p$")
    ax2.set_aspect("equal")
    ax2.set_xlim(0, 1.05)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 1.05)
    ax2.set_xlabel(r"$|W(p)|/(2\sqrt p)$  (what the witness reads)")
    ax2.set_ylabel(r"$|A(\nu)|/(2\sqrt p)$  (what it cannot read)")
    ax2.set_title("The two-leg trade-off: a big signal costs you the twin")
    ax2.legend(fontsize=9, loc="lower left")

    fig.suptitle("The Weil bound is an identity, not an estimate", fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("two_squares.png", dpi=150)
    print("wrote two_squares.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: Breaking the Residue Dial, and the Shadow It Leaves
visualizations.description: A side-by-side strip plot contrasting two views of the statistic against the residue class p mod 8. On the left, the raw values W(p) scatter across the whole Weil band within each class -- so no function of p mod 8 can reproduce them, which is precisely the refutation of the dial hypothesis that distinguishes this witness from every earlier one; the classes 3 and 7 collapse to the single value zero, the supersingular blind spot. On the right, the same data reduced mod 8 collapses to a single point per class, exposing the residual dial: the low-order bits of the statistic are publicly computable from N and therefore information-free, so everything of value lives in exactly the high-order bits that the Weil bound confines.
visualizations.code:
"""
Visualization: the dial is broken (but its shadow survives).

A statistic F is a "residue dial" mod 8 if F(N) depends only on N mod 8; such a
statistic is worthless as a factoring witness because its value is readable off N
itself.  This figure contrasts two views of the Jacobi-signed circle count W:

Left  : W(p) plotted against p mod 8 as a strip plot.  Inside each residue class
        the values are spread out over the whole Weil band -- so no function of
        p mod 8 can reproduce W.  The dial is broken.
Right : W(p) mod 8 plotted the same way.  Here the columns collapse to single
        points (6 for p = 1 mod 8, 2 for p = 5 mod 8): the *low-order bits* of the
        statistic ARE a dial, i.e. publicly computable and information-free.
        Everything of value lives in the high-order bits, and those are exactly
        the ones the Weil bound confines to a window of width O(sqrt p).

Requires: matplotlib, numpy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = [True] * limit
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def circle_weight_prime(p: int) -> int:
    return sum(legendre(x * (1 - x * x) % p, p) for x in range(p))


def main(cutoff: int = 1500) -> None:
    rng = random.Random(11)
    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(cutoff) if p > 2]
    ws = {p: circle_weight_prime(p) for p in ps}

    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.4))
    classes = [1, 3, 5, 7]
    colours = {1: "#4fd1c5", 3: "#4a5568", 5: "#f78da7", 7: "#4a5568"}

    for k, c in enumerate(classes):
        sub = [p for p in ps if p % 8 == c]
        jitter = [k + rng.uniform(-0.18, 0.18) for _ in sub]
        ax1.scatter(jitter, [ws[p] for p in sub], s=16, color=colours[c], alpha=0.8)
        ax2.scatter(jitter, [ws[p] % 8 for p in sub], s=16, color=colours[c], alpha=0.8)

    xs = np.linspace(-0.5, 3.5, 10)
    ax1.plot(xs, [0] * len(xs), color="#94a3b8", lw=0.6)
    for ax, title, ylab in (
        (ax1, "$W(p)$ within each class of $p \\bmod 8$:\nno dial can do this",
         "$W(p)$"),
        (ax2, "$W(p) \\bmod 8$ within each class:\nthe low bits are a dial",
         "$W(p) \\bmod 8$"),
    ):
        ax.set_xticks(range(4))
        ax.set_xticklabels([f"$p \\equiv {c}$" for c in classes])
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11)
        ax.set_ylabel(ylab)

    ax1.annotate("classes 3 and 7: identically zero\n(no signal at all)",
                 xy=(1, 0), xytext=(1.15, max(ws.values()) * 0.55), fontsize=9,
                 color="#e9eef8",
                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#94a3b8", lw=1))

    fig.suptitle("Escaping the residue dial -- and what remains of it", fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("dial_broken.png", dpi=150)
    print(f"{len(ps)} primes plotted; distinct values for p = 1 mod 8: "
          f"{len({ws[p] for p in ps if p % 8 == 1})}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_layout:
# A Circle That Refuses to Tell You Its Secret ### Or: what happens when you weight a point count by a sign Take a very large odd number $N$, promised to be a product of two primes, $N = pq$. Factoring it is hard. But is there some cheap, natural quantity attached to $N$ — a count, a sum, a statistic — that quietly *knows* something about $p$ and $q$? This notebook follows one candidate all the way to the end of its life. It is a story with a genuinely surprising middle (the candidate does something no earlier candidate managed) and a beautiful, inevitable ending (it dies anyway, of a cause we can name exactly). Along the way we will accidentally prove Fermat's two-square theorem. --- ## 1. Circles in clock arithmetic Do arithmetic modulo $N$. The unit circle becomes a finite scatter of dots: $$S(N) \;=\; \{(x,y) \in (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^2 \;:\; x^2 + y^2 = 1\}.$$ Counting those dots is the obvious first move — and it fails immediately, for a reason worth naming. > **Definition (residue dial).** A statistic $F$ is a *residue dial* modulo $m$ if $F(N) = f(N \bmod m)$ for some function $f$. A dial is worthless as a factoring witness: you can read it off $N$ itself in constant time. And the plain circle count is a dial in disguise — over a prime $p$ it has exactly $p - \chi(-1)$ points, where $\chi(-1) = \pm 1$ according to $p \bmod 4$, so for $N=pq$ the count is $N$ times a correction determined by $N \bmod 4$.
Why the plain count is $p - \chi(-1)$ (click to expand) Over a field of odd characteristic, the number of $y$ with $y^2 = a$ equals $\chi(a)+1$, where $\chi$ is the quadratic character ($+1$ on nonzero squares, $-1$ on nonsquares, $0$ at $0$). So $$|S(p)| = \sum_x \bigl(\chi(1-x^2)+1\bigr) = p + \sum_x \chi(1-x^2).$$ The last sum is a standard quadratic-polynomial character sum: for a quadratic with distinct roots it equals $-\chi(\text{leading coefficient})$, here $-\chi(-1)$. Hence $|S(p)| = p - \chi(-1)$.
**The idea that breaks the dial:** don't count each point as $1$. Count it with a **sign** — the Jacobi symbol of its $x$-coordinate: $$\boxed{\;W(N) \;=\; \sum_{(x,y) \in S(N)} \left(\frac{x}{N}\right).\;}$$ Roughly half the points now contribute $+1$ and half $-1$. Massive cancellation is built in, and what survives is a delicate residue of arithmetic bias. Play with it before we prove anything about it. {{interactive_demo:0}} Things worth doing in the widget above: * Set $N = 21 = 3 \cdot 7$. The answer is $0$. Now try $N = 15, 33, 39, 51$ — all zero. Something systematic is happening whenever a factor is $\equiv 3 \pmod 4$. * Set $N = 85 = 5\cdot 17$ and read the multiplicativity panel: $W(5) = 2$, $W(17) = -2$, and $W(85) = -4$. The statistic *factors*. * Compare $N = 17$ and $N = 41$. Both are $\equiv 1 \pmod 8$, yet $W(17) = -2$ and $W(41) = -10$. **No function of $N \bmod 8$ can produce both.** The dial is broken. --- ## 2. The circle collapses to a curve The two-dimensional sum is secretly one-dimensional. > **Theorem (Collapse identity).** For every odd prime $p$, > $$W(p) \;=\; \sum_{x \bmod p} \chi\bigl(x(1-x^2)\bigr).$$
Proof (two lines, click to reveal) Fix $x$ and sum over $y$: the number of $y$ with $y^2 = 1-x^2$ is $\chi(1-x^2)+1$, so the inner sum contributes $\chi(x)\bigl(\chi(1-x^2)+1\bigr)$. Expanding and using multiplicativity of $\chi$, $$W(p) = \sum_x \chi\bigl(x(1-x^2)\bigr) + \sum_x \chi(x),$$ and the second sum vanishes because a nontrivial character sums to zero over the whole group. $\blacksquare$
This is a big deal computationally — it drops the cost from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$ — and an even bigger deal structurally. The polynomial $x(1-x^2) = -(x^3-x)$ is a cubic with distinct roots, so the right-hand side is (up to sign) the **trace of Frobenius of the elliptic curve $y^2 = x^3 - x$**. Our innocent signed dot count is a point count on a genus-one curve. That fact will kill it later. {{algorithm:0}} --- ## 3. It factors — and that is the problem > **Theorem (Multiplicativity).** If $\gcd(m,n) = 1$ then $W(mn) = W(m)W(n)$. In particular $W(pq) = W(p)W(q)$.
Proof sketch: Chinese Remainder Theorem, twice A point of the circle mod $mn$ is exactly a pair of points, one mod $m$ and one mod $n$: applying the reduction homomorphisms shows the necessity, and injectivity of the CRT map shows the sufficiency. Meanwhile the Jacobi symbol splits along the modulus, $\left(\frac{x}{mn}\right) = \left(\frac{x}{m}\right)\left(\frac{x}{n}\right)$. So the summand factors, and the sum over a product set of a product of functions is the product of the sums. $\blacksquare$
Read this twice, because it cuts both ways. * **Good news.** Unlike a dial, $W$ is genuinely *factor-dependent* — its value is literally manufactured out of data belonging to $p$ and to $q$ separately. * **Bad news.** It is a **symmetric product**. An attacker who learns $W(N) = W(p)W(q)$ has learned one integer that entangles the two. Splitting a product of two unknowns is the original problem in miniature. And there is worse. Substituting $x \mapsto -x$ multiplies the cubic sum by $\chi(-1)$, so: > **Theorem (Vanishing).** If $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ then $W(p) = 0$; hence $W(N) = 0$ whenever any prime factor of $N$ is $\equiv 3 \pmod 4$. Three quarters of all semiprimes are annihilated outright. Let's count exactly how bad this is. {{demo:1}} Roughly $79\%$ of semiprimes below $20000$ return zero, and among the survivors the same value is shared by around six different factorisations on average. As a channel, this statistic is carrying about $6$ bits where $11$ bits of factorisation live. --- ## 4. The wall: why the noise floor is exactly $\sqrt{N}$ Here is the deep reason. Introduce the **quadratic twists** $$A(d) \;=\; \sum_{x \bmod p} \chi(x^3 - dx),$$ so that $W(p) = A(1)$ when $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. A short averaging argument gives an *exact* second moment, and the Weil bound falls out of it with no algebraic geometry at all. > **Theorem (Exact second moment).** For $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, $\displaystyle\sum_{d \bmod p} A(d)^2 = 2p(p-1)$. > > **Corollary (Weil floor).** $W(p)^2 \le 4p$, i.e. $|W(p)| \le 2\sqrt p$; hence $|W(N)| \le 4\sqrt N$ for semiprimes.
Proof of the second moment (click to reveal the computation) Expand $A(d)^2$ and swap the order of summation, using $\chi(x^3-dx)\chi(y^3-dy) = \chi(xy)\,\chi\bigl((x^2-d)(y^2-d)\bigr)$: $$\sum_d A(d)^2 = \sum_x\sum_y \chi(xy)\sum_d \chi\bigl((d-x^2)(d-y^2)\bigr).$$ The inner sum is a quadratic character sum: it equals $p-1$ when $x^2=y^2$ and $-1$ otherwise, i.e. $p\cdot[x^2=y^2] - 1$. The $-1$ part contributes $-\bigl(\sum_x\chi(x)\bigr)^2 = 0$. For the rest, the diagonal $y = \pm x$ contributes $\chi(x^2) + \chi(-x^2) = 2$ for each $x \ne 0$ (this is where $p \equiv 1 \bmod 4$ is used), giving $p \cdot 2(p-1)$. $\blacksquare$
Proof of the Weil bound from it (click to reveal) Scaling: substituting $x = cu$ shows $A(c^2 e) = \chi(c)A(e)$, so $A(c^2)^2 = A(1)^2$ for every $c \ne 0$. Summing over the $p-1$ nonzero $c$, and noting that $c \mapsto c^2$ is at most $2$-to-$1$ while $A(d)^2 \ge 0$, $$(p-1)A(1)^2 = \sum_{c\ne 0} A(c^2)^2 \le 2\sum_d A(d)^2 = 4p(p-1).$$ Cancel $p-1$. $\blacksquare$
{{algorithm:1}} How tight is it really? Not asymptotically tight — *numerically* tight, again and again. {{visualization:0}} --- ## 5. The bound is an identity: the conservation law The reason the bound is attained so often is that it isn't really a bound. Let $\nu$ be any quadratic nonresidue mod $p$. > **Theorem (Jacobsthal identity).** For $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, > $$A(1)^2 + A(\nu)^2 \;=\; 4p.$$ The residue twist and the nonresidue twist are the two legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse $2\sqrt p$. Big signal in one leg $\Rightarrow$ small signal in the other, always, with $4p$ conserved.
Proof: push the moment forward along squaring, twice Let $F(d) = A(d)^2$. Since the fibre of $c \mapsto c^2$ over $d$ has $\chi(d)+1$ elements, $$\sum_c F(c^2) = \sum_d (\chi(d)+1)F(d), \qquad \sum_c F(\nu c^2) = \sum_d (1-\chi(d))F(d),$$ the second after substituting $d \mapsto \nu^{-1}d$ and using $\chi(\nu) = -1$. But by the scaling law the left-hand sides are $(p-1)A(1)^2$ and $(p-1)A(\nu)^2$. Adding, the character weights cancel exactly and the right-hand side becomes $2\sum_d F(d) = 4p(p-1)$. Cancel $p-1$. $\blacksquare$
Watch the conservation law happen: {{interactive_demo:1}} Now divide the identity by $4$. Both $A(1)$ and $A(\nu)$ are even (a reflection-pairing argument), so with $a = W(p)/2$ and $b = A(\nu)/2$: > **Theorem (Fermat's two-square theorem, with explicit witnesses).** For every prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, > $$p = a^2 + b^2, \qquad a = \tfrac{1}{2}W(p),$$ > and moreover $a$ is **odd** — equivalently $W(p) \equiv 2 \pmod 4$.
Why the odd leg? A parity count (click to reveal) Pair up $x$ with $-x$: the summand of $W(p)$ is invariant, so $W(p) = 2S$ where $S$ is the sum over the "lower half" $H$ of the nonzero residues, $|H| = (p-1)/2$. Each term lies in $\{0,\pm1\}$, so $S \equiv \sum_{x\in H} f(x)^2 \pmod 2$, and $f(x)^2 = 1$ except when $x(1-x^2) = 0$, i.e. $x \in \{0,1,-1\}$. Of these, only $x=1$ lies in $H$. Hence $S \equiv |H| - 1 = \frac{p-1}{2}-1$, which is odd because $4 \mid p-1$. $\blacksquare$
So the "mysterious, erratic" statistic was never mysterious. It is **twice the odd leg of the Gaussian decomposition of $p$**: $17 = 1^2+4^2$ and $W(17)=-2$; $41=5^2+4^2$ and $W(41)=-10$; $173=13^2+2^2$ and $W(173)=26$; $293=17^2+2^2$ and $W(293)=34$. {{visualization:1}} That picture is the whole verdict in one image. A witness that reads $W(p)$ is reading **one coordinate of a point pinned to a circle** — a projection of a conserved quantity. There is no direction in which the signal can grow. --- ## 6. The dial is broken. It doesn't help. Let's be scrupulous about the one genuinely new thing here. > **Theorem (Not a residue dial).** There is no function $f$ with $W(p) = f(p \bmod 8)$ for all primes: $17 \equiv 41 \equiv 1 \pmod 8$ but $W(17) = -2 \ne -10 = W(41)$. Likewise no $f$ with $W(p) = f(p \bmod 4)$ ($W(13) = -6$, $W(17) = -2$), and no $f$ with $W(N) = f(N \bmod 8)$ at composite level ($W(21) = 0$, $W(85) = -4$, both $N \equiv 5 \bmod 8$). Every earlier weighted circle count in this family collapsed to a dial. This one does not. But notice what *does* remain a dial: {{visualization:2}} The **low-order bits** of $W$ are a dial — $W(p) \bmod 8$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$ — and everything of value lives in the high-order bits, which are exactly the ones the Weil bound confines to a window of width $O(\sqrt p)$. That is the trap in one sentence: *the part you can compute for free is public, and the part that is private is bounded.* Is there any usable signal in what's left? Test it honestly, with a permutation null. {{algorithm:2}} Across forty semiprimes with both factors $\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, correlations of $W(N)$ with $p$, $q$, $p+q$, $|p-q|$ all sit inside the null distribution. **Factor-dependent, yes. Structured, no.** --- ## 7. The full verification suite Everything claimed above, checked numerically end to end: the collapse identity against the brute-force definition, multiplicativity, vanishing, exact parity, the second moment, the Weil bound, the Jacobsthal identity, the two-square decomposition, the dial refutations, the blind families, and the permutation test. {{demo:0}} --- ## 8. What actually killed it Three walls, stacked: | Barrier | Statement | Why it is fatal | |---|---|---| | **Cost** | Evaluating $W(N)$ takes $\Theta(N)$ operations | Worse than trial division ($O(\sqrt N)$); and the fast route needs $W(p), W(q)$ — i.e. the answer | | **Symmetry** | $W(N) = W(p)W(q)$ | The factors enter only through an entangled, symmetric product | | **Weil floor** | $\lvert W(N)\rvert \le 4\sqrt N$ | $O(\sqrt N)$ possible values against $\Theta(N/\log^2 N)$ factorisations: irreparable collisions | And the general principle, which is why this is a structural verdict rather than one failed experiment: > **Principle.** Summing $y$ away turns *any* character-weighted circle count $\sum_{x^2+y^2=1}\psi(x)$ into $\sum_x \psi(x)\bigl(1+\chi(1-x^2)\bigr)$, i.e. a **Jacobi sum** — and Jacobi sums have absolute value exactly $\sqrt p$. **The square-root floor is a property of the circle, not of the weight.** Changing the character is rearranging deck chairs. To escape you would have to change the geometry. --- ## 9. Where to go next * **Every weight is at the floor.** Conjecture: for a character $\psi$ of order $d$, $|W_\psi(p)| \le d\sqrt p$, with $W_\psi$ a $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_d]$-combination of Jacobi sums. The second-moment machinery used above is character-agnostic, so this looks reachable. * **Equidistribution on the Weil circle.** Conjecture: $W(N)/(4\sqrt N)$ has a Sato–Tate-type limiting law (a pushforward of two arcsine laws), so the statistic carries $O(1)$ bits about $p$ versus $q$. * **Change the geometry.** Higher-genus or non-CM families, where the point count is not governed by a single Frobenius eigenvalue pair — subject always to the binding constraint that a useful witness must be computable in time $o(\sqrt N)$. ### Further reading * [Quadratic residues and the Legendre symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_symbol) * [The Jacobi symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobi_symbol) * [Jacobsthal sums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobsthal_sum) * [Fermat's theorem on sums of two squares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_theorem_on_sums_of_two_squares) * [Hasse's theorem on elliptic curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasse%27s_theorem_on_elliptic_curves) — the general form of the $2\sqrt p$ ceiling * [The Sato–Tate conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sato%E2%80%93Tate_conjecture) — what the spread inside the ceiling should look like --- **The consolation prize.** We set out to build a factoring witness and ended up with a clean, fully explicit proof that every prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ is a sum of two squares — with the odd leg handed over as half a signed count of lattice points on a circle. The circle would not give up the secret we asked for. It gave up a better one, and explained, in the sharpest possible terms, why the first is safe.

-- ===== Catalog/Tropical/JacobiSignedWeilFloorCore.lean =====
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Jacobi-signed circle count: core structure (JACSIGN)

For an odd prime `p` let `χ = quadraticChar (ZMod p)` be the Legendre character and let

`S(p) = {(x, y) ∈ (ZMod p)² : x² + y² = 1}`

be the unit circle over `ZMod p`.  The *Jacobi-signed circle count* is the character
weighted point count

`circleWeight p = ∑_{(x,y) ∈ S(p)} χ(x)`.

This file proves the basic structure of this weight:

* `JacSign.circleWeight_eq_W` : the geometric weight collapses to the **cubic character sum**
  `W p = ∑_x χ(x(1 - x²))`, i.e. the trace of Frobenius of the curve `y² = x - x³`
  (up to sign).
* `JacSign.W_neg_reflect` : the reflection identity `W p = χ(-1) · W p`.
* `JacSign.W_eq_zero_of_three_mod_four` : `W p = 0` whenever `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` — the
  supersingular half of the primes carries **no** signal at all.
* `JacSign.W_even` : `W p` is always even, so the weight can never be an odd number;
  this matches the observed data `-2, -10, 6, -18, 14, 22`.

These are the structural facts underlying the JACSIGN experiment; the Weil bound
`W p ^ 2 ≤ 4 p` is proved in `JacobiSignedWeilFloorBound.lean`.
-/

open Finset

namespace JacSign

/-- The character sum `W p = ∑_x χ(x (1 - x²))`, where `χ` is the Legendre character. -/
noncomputable def W (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ℤ :=
  ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * (1 - x ^ 2))

/-- The Jacobi-signed circle count: the points of the unit circle `x² + y² = 1` over
`ZMod p`, each weighted by the Legendre symbol of its `x`-coordinate. -/
noncomputable def circleWeight (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ℤ :=
  ∑ x : ZMod p, ∑ y : ZMod p, if x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = 1 then quadraticChar (ZMod p) x else 0

variable (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]

/-- The geometric (circle) weight equals the cubic character sum `W p`. -/
theorem circleWeight_eq_W (hp : p ≠ 2) : circleWeight p = W p := by
  have hF : ringChar (ZMod p) ≠ 2 := by rw [ZMod.ringChar_zmod_n]; exact hp
  have key : ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ((univ.filter (fun y : ZMod p => y ^ 2 = a)).card : ℤ) = quadraticChar (ZMod p) a + 1 := by
    intro a
    simpa [Set.toFinset_setOf] using quadraticChar_card_sqrts (F := ZMod p) hF a
  have step : ∀ x : ZMod p,
      (∑ y : ZMod p, if x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = 1 then quadraticChar (ZMod p) x else 0)
        = quadraticChar (ZMod p) x * (quadraticChar (ZMod p) (1 - x ^ 2) + 1) := by
    intro x
    rw [Finset.sum_ite, Finset.sum_const, Finset.sum_const]
    have hset : (univ.filter (fun y : ZMod p => x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = 1))
        = (univ.filter (fun y : ZMod p => y ^ 2 = 1 - x ^ 2)) := by
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro y _
      constructor <;> intro h <;> linear_combination h
    rw [hset, nsmul_eq_mul, smul_zero, add_zero, ← key (1 - x ^ 2), mul_comm]
  simp only [circleWeight, step, mul_add, mul_one, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  rw [quadraticChar_sum_zero hF, add_zero]
  simp [W, map_mul]

/-- Reflection identity: replacing `x` by `-x` multiplies the summand by `χ(-1)`. -/
theorem W_neg_reflect : W p = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) * W p := by
  have hrefl : ∀ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * (1 - x ^ 2))
      = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) * quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((-x) * (1 - (-x) ^ 2)) := by
    intro x
    rw [← map_mul]
    congr 1
    ring
  calc W p = ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) *
              quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((-x) * (1 - (-x) ^ 2)) := by
        rw [W]; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => hrefl x
    _ = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) * W p := by
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
        congr 1
        exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.neg (ZMod p)) _ _ fun x => rfl

theorem chi_neg_one_eq_neg_one (hp : p % 4 = 3) : quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) = -1 := by
  rw [quadraticChar_neg_one_iff_not_isSquare, ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff]
  simp [hp]

theorem chi_neg_one_eq_one (hp : p % 4 = 1) : quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) = 1 := by
  have hne : (-1 : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := neg_ne_zero.mpr one_ne_zero
  rw [quadraticChar_one_iff_isSquare hne, ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff]
  omega

/-- **Half of all primes carry no signal.** For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` the Jacobi-signed
circle count vanishes identically. -/
theorem W_eq_zero_of_three_mod_four (hp : p % 4 = 3) : W p = 0 := by
  have h := W_neg_reflect p
  rw [chi_neg_one_eq_neg_one p hp] at h
  linarith

/-- The "lower half" of the nonzero residues: one representative of each pair
`{x, -x}`. -/
def halfSet (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : Finset (ZMod p) :=
  (univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => 2 * x.val < p)).erase 0

/-- **A reflection-parity lemma.** Any function on `ZMod p` that is invariant under
`x ↦ -x` and vanishes at `0` has total sum twice its sum over the lower half: the
nonzero arguments pair up. -/
theorem sum_eq_two_mul_half (hp : p ≠ 2) (f : ZMod p → ℤ)
    (hfneg : ∀ x : ZMod p, f (-x) = f x) (hf0 : f 0 = 0) :
    (∑ x : ZMod p, f x) = 2 * ∑ x ∈ halfSet p, f x := by
  have hprime := (Fact.out : p.Prime)
  have hodd : p % 2 = 1 := hprime.eq_two_or_odd.resolve_left hp
  have hp3 : 3 ≤ p := by
    rcases hprime.two_le.lt_or_eq with h | h
    · omega
    · omega
  haveI : NeZero p := ⟨by omega⟩
  set A : Finset (ZMod p) := univ.filter (fun x => 2 * x.val < p) with hA
  have hsplit : (∑ x : ZMod p, f x)
      = ∑ x ∈ A, f x + ∑ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => ¬ (2 * x.val < p)), f x :=
    (Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not univ _ f).symm
  have hval0 : ∀ x : ZMod p, x.val = 0 ↔ x = 0 := fun x => ZMod.val_eq_zero x
  have hne : ∀ x : ZMod p, x ≠ 0 → 2 * x.val ≠ p := by
    intro x _ h
    omega
  have hB : ∑ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => ¬ (2 * x.val < p)), f x
      = ∑ x ∈ A.erase 0, f x := by
    refine Finset.sum_nbij' (i := fun x => -x) (j := fun x => -x) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro a ha
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, not_lt] at ha
      have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := by
        intro h; rw [h] at ha; simp at ha; omega
      haveI : NeZero a := ⟨ha0⟩
      have hv : (-a).val = p - a.val := ZMod.val_neg_of_ne_zero a
      have hlt : a.val < p := ZMod.val_lt a
      have hne' : 2 * a.val ≠ p := hne a ha0
      refine Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · simpa [neg_eq_zero] using ha0
      · simp only [hA, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, hv]
        omega
    · intro a ha
      have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp ha).1
      have ha' := (Finset.mem_erase.mp ha).2
      simp only [hA, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at ha'
      haveI : NeZero a := ⟨ha0⟩
      have hv : (-a).val = p - a.val := ZMod.val_neg_of_ne_zero a
      have hlt : a.val < p := ZMod.val_lt a
      have hpos : 0 < a.val := by
        rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos a.val with h | h
        · exact absurd ((hval0 a).mp h) ha0
        · exact h
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, not_lt, hv]
      omega
    · intro a _; simp
    · intro a _; simp
    · intro a _; exact (hfneg a).symm
  have hA0 : ∑ x ∈ A, f x = ∑ x ∈ A.erase 0, f x := by
    by_cases h0 : (0 : ZMod p) ∈ A
    · rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase A f h0, hf0, zero_add]
    · rw [Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem h0]
  rw [hsplit, hB, hA0, halfSet, ← hA]
  ring

/-- The total sum of a reflection-invariant function vanishing at `0` is even. -/
theorem sum_even_of_neg_invariant (hp : p ≠ 2) (f : ZMod p → ℤ)
    (hfneg : ∀ x : ZMod p, f (-x) = f x) (hf0 : f 0 = 0) :
    (2 : ℤ) ∣ ∑ x : ZMod p, f x :=
  ⟨_, sum_eq_two_mul_half p hp f hfneg hf0⟩

/-- The Jacobi-signed weight is always even; this matches every observed value
(`-2, -10, 6, -18, 14, 22, 34, ...`). -/
theorem W_even (hp : p ≠ 2) : (2 : ℤ) ∣ W p := by
  have hprime := (Fact.out : p.Prime)
  have hodd : p % 2 = 1 := hprime.eq_two_or_odd.resolve_left hp
  by_cases h4 : p % 4 = 3
  · rw [W_eq_zero_of_three_mod_four p h4]; exact dvd_zero 2
  have h1 : p % 4 = 1 := by
    have := hprime.two_le
    omega
  refine sum_even_of_neg_invariant p hp (fun x => quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * (1 - x ^ 2)))
    (fun x => ?_) (by simp)
  show quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((-x) * (1 - (-x) ^ 2)) = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * (1 - x ^ 2))
  have hx : quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((-x) * (1 - (-x) ^ 2))
      = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) * quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * (1 - x ^ 2)) := by
    rw [← map_mul]; congr 1; ring
  rw [hx, chi_neg_one_eq_one p h1, one_mul]

end JacSign

-- ===== Catalog/Tropical/JacobiSignedWeilFloorBound.lean =====
import Tropical.JacobiSignedWeilFloorCore

/-!
# The Weil floor for the Jacobi-signed circle count

This file proves, completely elementarily (no algebraic geometry, no Hasse bound
imported), the **Weil bound**

`W p ^ 2 ≤ 4 * p`

for the Jacobi-signed circle count `W p = ∑_x χ(x(1-x²))` of
`JacobiSignedWeilFloorCore.lean`.  Equivalently `|W p| ≤ 2 √p`: the JACSIGN
statistic sits exactly at the square-root noise floor of a character sum.

The proof is a second-moment (averaging over quadratic twists) argument:

* `JacSign.chiSum_quadratic` : `∑_d χ((d-a)(d-b)) = p-1` if `a = b` and `-1` otherwise;
* `JacSign.A p d = ∑_x χ(x³ - d x)` is the trace of Frobenius of `y² = x³ - d x`;
* `JacSign.A_sq_scale` : `A p (c²) = χ(c) · A p 1` — all *square* twists carry the
  same squared trace;
* `JacSign.moment` : `∑_d (A p d)² = 2 p (p-1)` — the exact second moment;
* since squaring is at most `2`-to-`1`, the `p-1` scalings contribute
  `(p-1) · (A p 1)² ≤ 2 · 2p(p-1)`, whence `(A p 1)² ≤ 4p`.
-/

open Finset

namespace JacSign

variable (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]

/-- `∑_u χ(u² - u) = -1`: the basic nontrivial quadratic character sum. -/
theorem chiSum_sq_sub_self (hp : p ≠ 2) :
    ∑ u : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (u ^ 2 - u) = -1 := by
  have hF : ringChar (ZMod p) ≠ 2 := by rw [ZMod.ringChar_zmod_n]; exact hp
  have h1 : ∑ u : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (u ^ 2 - u)
      = ∑ u ∈ univ.erase (0 : ZMod p), quadraticChar (ZMod p) (u ^ 2 - u) := by
    rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ (Finset.mem_univ (0 : ZMod p))]; simp
  have h2 : ∀ u ∈ univ.erase (0 : ZMod p),
      quadraticChar (ZMod p) (u ^ 2 - u) = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (1 - u⁻¹) := by
    intro u hu
    have hu0 : u ≠ 0 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp hu).1
    have h : u ^ 2 - u = u ^ 2 * (1 - u⁻¹) := by field_simp
    rw [h, map_mul, quadraticChar_sq_one' hu0, one_mul]
  rw [h1, Finset.sum_congr rfl h2]
  have h3 : ∑ u ∈ univ.erase (0 : ZMod p), quadraticChar (ZMod p) (1 - u⁻¹)
      = ∑ v ∈ univ.erase (1 : ZMod p), quadraticChar (ZMod p) v := by
    refine Finset.sum_nbij' (i := fun u => 1 - u⁻¹) (j := fun v => (1 - v)⁻¹) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro a ha
      have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp ha).1
      simp only [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_univ, and_true]
      intro h
      have hinv : a⁻¹ = 0 := by linear_combination -h
      exact ha0 (by simpa using inv_eq_zero.mp hinv)
    · intro v hv
      have hv1 : v ≠ 1 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp hv).1
      simp only [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_univ, and_true]
      exact inv_ne_zero (sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm hv1))
    · intro a ha
      have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp ha).1
      show (1 - (1 - a⁻¹))⁻¹ = a
      rw [show (1 : ZMod p) - (1 - a⁻¹) = a⁻¹ by ring, inv_inv]
    · intro v hv
      have hv1 : v ≠ 1 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp hv).1
      show 1 - ((1 - v)⁻¹)⁻¹ = v
      rw [inv_inv]; ring
    · intro a _; rfl
  rw [h3]
  have h4 := quadraticChar_sum_zero (F := ZMod p) hF
  have h5 : quadraticChar (ZMod p) 1
      + ∑ v ∈ univ.erase (1 : ZMod p), quadraticChar (ZMod p) v = 0 := by
    rw [Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ (Finset.mem_univ (1 : ZMod p))]; exact h4
  rw [MulChar.map_one] at h5
  linarith

/-- The character sum of a quadratic polynomial with roots `a`, `b`. -/
theorem chiSum_quadratic (hp : p ≠ 2) (a b : ZMod p) :
    ∑ d : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((d - a) * (d - b))
      = if a = b then (p : ℤ) - 1 else -1 := by
  by_cases hab : a = b
  · subst hab
    rw [if_pos rfl]
    have hval : ∀ d : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((d - a) * (d - a))
        = if d = a then 0 else 1 := by
      intro d
      by_cases hd : d = a
      · simp [hd]
      · rw [if_neg hd, ← sq]
        exact quadraticChar_sq_one' (sub_ne_zero.mpr hd)
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => hval d, Finset.sum_ite]
    have h : (univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => ¬ x = a)) = univ.erase a := by
      ext x; simp [Finset.mem_erase, and_comm]
    have hp2 := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
    rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.sum_const, h,
      Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ a), Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card]
    simp only [smul_zero, zero_add, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    push_cast [Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ p)]
    ring
  · have hba : b - a ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm hab)
    have hre : ∑ d : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((d - a) * (d - b))
        = ∑ u : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p)
            ((((Equiv.mulLeft₀ (b - a) hba).trans (Equiv.addLeft a)) u - a) *
             (((Equiv.mulLeft₀ (b - a) hba).trans (Equiv.addLeft a)) u - b)) :=
      (Fintype.sum_equiv ((Equiv.mulLeft₀ (b - a) hba).trans (Equiv.addLeft a)) _ _
        fun u => rfl).symm
    rw [hre]
    have hval : ∀ u : ZMod p,
        ((((Equiv.mulLeft₀ (b - a) hba).trans (Equiv.addLeft a)) u - a) *
         (((Equiv.mulLeft₀ (b - a) hba).trans (Equiv.addLeft a)) u - b))
          = (b - a) ^ 2 * (u ^ 2 - u) := by
      intro u
      show (a + (b - a) * u - a) * (a + (b - a) * u - b) = (b - a) ^ 2 * (u ^ 2 - u)
      ring
    simp only [hval, map_mul, quadraticChar_sq_one' hba, one_mul]
    rw [chiSum_sq_sub_self p hp, if_neg hab]

/-- `A p d` is the character sum of the quadratic twist `y² = x³ - d x`
(the negative of its trace of Frobenius). -/
noncomputable def A (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (d : ZMod p) : ℤ :=
  ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x ^ 3 - d * x)

theorem chi_cube (x : ZMod p) : quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x ^ 3) = quadraticChar (ZMod p) x := by
  rw [map_pow]
  rcases quadraticChar_isQuadratic (ZMod p) x with h | h | h <;> rw [h] <;> norm_num

theorem A_zero (hp : p ≠ 2) : A p 0 = 0 := by
  have hF : ringChar (ZMod p) ≠ 2 := by rw [ZMod.ringChar_zmod_n]; exact hp
  simp only [A, zero_mul, sub_zero, chi_cube]
  exact quadraticChar_sum_zero hF

/-- All square twists have the same character sum up to the sign `χ(c)`. -/
theorem A_sq_scale {c : ZMod p} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    A p (c ^ 2) = quadraticChar (ZMod p) c * A p 1 := by
  have hre : A p (c ^ 2) = ∑ u : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((c * u) ^ 3 - c ^ 2 * (c * u)) := by
    rw [A]
    exact (Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.mulLeft₀ c hc) _ _ fun u => rfl).symm
  rw [hre, A, Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun u _ => ?_
  rw [show (c * u) ^ 3 - c ^ 2 * (c * u) = c ^ 3 * (u ^ 3 - 1 * u) by ring, map_mul, chi_cube]

theorem inner_T (hp : p ≠ 2) (h1 : p % 4 = 1) (x : ZMod p) :
    (∑ y : ZMod p, if x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 then quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) else 0)
      = if x = 0 then 0 else 2 := by
  have hchi1 : quadraticChar (ZMod p) (-1) = 1 := chi_neg_one_eq_one p h1
  have hset : (univ.filter (fun y : ZMod p => x ^ 2 = y ^ 2)) = {x, -x} := by
    ext y
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_insert,
      Finset.mem_singleton]
    constructor
    · intro h
      rcases sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg.mp h.symm with h' | h'
      · exact Or.inl h'
      · exact Or.inr h'
    · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> ring
  rw [← Finset.sum_filter, hset]
  by_cases hx : x = 0
  · subst hx; simp
  · rw [if_neg hx]
    have hne : x ≠ -x := by
      intro h
      rcases (ZMod.neg_eq_self_iff x).mp h.symm with h' | h'
      · exact hx h'
      · have hodd : p % 2 = 1 := (Fact.out : p.Prime).eq_two_or_odd.resolve_left hp
        omega
    have e1 : quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * x) = 1 := by
      rw [← sq]; exact quadraticChar_sq_one' hx
    have e2 : quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * -x) = 1 := by
      rw [show x * -x = (-1) * x ^ 2 by ring, map_mul, hchi1, one_mul, quadraticChar_sq_one' hx]
    rw [Finset.sum_pair hne, e1, e2]
    norm_num

/-- **The exact second moment over all quadratic twists.** -/
theorem moment (hp : p ≠ 2) (h1 : p % 4 = 1) :
    ∑ d : ZMod p, (A p d) ^ 2 = 2 * (p : ℤ) * ((p : ℤ) - 1) := by
  have hF : ringChar (ZMod p) ≠ 2 := by rw [ZMod.ringChar_zmod_n]; exact hp
  have hp2 := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
  have hstep1 : ∀ d : ZMod p, (A p d) ^ 2
      = ∑ x : ZMod p, ∑ y : ZMod p,
          quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) *
            quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((d - x ^ 2) * (d - y ^ 2)) := by
    intro d
    rw [sq, A, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
    rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul]
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => hstep1 d, Finset.sum_comm]
  have hswap : ∀ x : ZMod p, (∑ d : ZMod p, ∑ y : ZMod p,
        quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) * quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((d - x ^ 2) * (d - y ^ 2)))
      = ∑ y : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) *
          (if x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 then (p : ℤ) - 1 else -1) := by
    intro x
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, chiSum_quadratic p hp (x ^ 2) (y ^ 2)]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => hswap x]
  have hterm : ∀ x y : ZMod p,
      quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) * (if x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 then (p : ℤ) - 1 else -1)
        = (if x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 then quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) else 0) * (p : ℤ)
          - quadraticChar (ZMod p) x * quadraticChar (ZMod p) y := by
    intro x y
    by_cases h : x ^ 2 = y ^ 2
    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, map_mul]; ring
    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h, map_mul]; ring
  simp only [hterm, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  have hT : ∑ x : ZMod p, ∑ y : ZMod p,
      (if x ^ 2 = y ^ 2 then quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x * y) else 0) * (p : ℤ)
      = 2 * ((p : ℤ) - 1) * (p : ℤ) := by
    simp only [← Finset.sum_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => inner_T p hp h1 x]
    congr 1
    rw [Finset.sum_ite]
    have h : (univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => ¬ x = 0)) = univ.erase 0 := by
      ext x; simp [Finset.mem_erase, and_comm]
    rw [h, Finset.sum_const, Finset.sum_const,
      Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ (0 : ZMod p)), Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card]
    simp only [smul_zero, zero_add, nsmul_eq_mul]
    push_cast [Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ p)]
    ring
  have hzero : ∑ x : ZMod p, ∑ y : ZMod p,
      quadraticChar (ZMod p) x * quadraticChar (ZMod p) y = 0 := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul_sum, quadraticChar_sum_zero hF, mul_zero]
  rw [hT, hzero, sub_zero]
  ring

/-- **The Weil floor.** The trace sum of `y² = x³ - x` obeys `|A| ≤ 2√p`. -/
theorem A_one_sq_le (hp : p ≠ 2) (h1 : p % 4 = 1) : (A p 1) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * (p : ℤ) := by
  have hp2 := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
  set F : ZMod p → ℤ := fun d => (A p d) ^ 2 with hFdef
  have hFnn : ∀ d, 0 ≤ F d := fun d => sq_nonneg _
  have hscale : ∀ c ∈ univ.erase (0 : ZMod p), F (c ^ 2) = (A p 1) ^ 2 := by
    intro c hc
    have hc0 : c ≠ 0 := (Finset.mem_erase.mp hc).1
    rw [hFdef]
    simp only
    rw [A_sq_scale p hc0, mul_pow, quadraticChar_sq_one hc0, one_mul]
  have hleft : ∑ c ∈ univ.erase (0 : ZMod p), F (c ^ 2) = ((p : ℤ) - 1) * (A p 1) ^ 2 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hscale, Finset.sum_const,
      Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ (0 : ZMod p)), Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card,
      nsmul_eq_mul]
    congr 1
    push_cast [Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ p)]
    ring
  have hfib : ∀ b : ZMod p,
      ((univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).filter (fun c => c ^ 2 = b)).card ≤ 2 := by
    intro b
    by_cases hemp : ((univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).filter (fun c => c ^ 2 = b)) = ∅
    · simp [hemp]
    · obtain ⟨c0, hc0⟩ := Finset.nonempty_of_ne_empty hemp
      have hsub : ((univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).filter (fun c => c ^ 2 = b)) ⊆ {c0, -c0} := by
        intro c hc
        have hcb : c ^ 2 = b := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hc).2
        have hc0b : c0 ^ 2 = b := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hc0).2
        have hcc : c ^ 2 = c0 ^ 2 := by rw [hcb, hc0b]
        rcases sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg.mp hcc with h | h
        · simp [h]
        · simp [h]
      calc ((univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).filter (fun c => c ^ 2 = b)).card
          ≤ ({c0, -c0} : Finset (ZMod p)).card := Finset.card_le_card hsub
        _ ≤ 2 := (Finset.card_insert_le _ _).trans (by simp)
  have hright : ∑ c ∈ univ.erase (0 : ZMod p), F (c ^ 2) ≤ 2 * ∑ d : ZMod p, F d := by
    rw [Finset.sum_comp F fun c : ZMod p => c ^ 2]
    have hle : ∑ b ∈ (univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).image (fun c : ZMod p => c ^ 2),
        ((univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).filter (fun c => c ^ 2 = b)).card • F b
        ≤ ∑ b ∈ (univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).image (fun c : ZMod p => c ^ 2), 2 * F b := by
      refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => ?_
      rw [nsmul_eq_mul]
      have hb := hFnn b
      have hcard : (((univ.erase (0 : ZMod p)).filter (fun c => c ^ 2 = b)).card : ℤ) ≤ 2 := by
        exact_mod_cast hfib b
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcard hb
    refine hle.trans ?_
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
      fun b _ _ => by positivity
  rw [hleft, moment p hp h1] at hright
  have hpos : (0 : ℤ) < (p : ℤ) - 1 := by
    have : (2 : ℤ) ≤ (p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hp2
    linarith
  nlinarith [hright, hpos]

/-- For `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` the Jacobi-signed circle count is the twist sum `A p 1`. -/
theorem W_eq_A_one (h1 : p % 4 = 1) : W p = A p 1 := by
  rw [W, A]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
  rw [show x * (1 - x ^ 2) = (-1) * (x ^ 3 - 1 * x) by ring, map_mul,
    chi_neg_one_eq_one p h1, one_mul]

/-- **The Weil floor for the Jacobi-signed circle count.**
For every odd prime `p`, `W p ^ 2 ≤ 4 p`, i.e. `|W p| ≤ 2 √p`. -/
theorem W_sq_le (hp : p ≠ 2) : (W p) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * (p : ℤ) := by
  have hp2 := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
  have hodd : p % 2 = 1 := (Fact.out : p.Prime).eq_two_or_odd.resolve_left hp
  by_cases h3 : p % 4 = 3
  · rw [W_eq_zero_of_three_mod_four p h3]
    have hnn : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (p : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg p
    nlinarith
  · have h1 : p % 4 = 1 := by omega
    rw [W_eq_A_one p h1]
    exact A_one_sq_le p hp h1

/-- The Weil floor in absolute-value form: `|W p| ≤ 2 √p`. -/
theorem abs_W_le (hp : p ≠ 2) : |(W p : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt p := by
  have h := W_sq_le p hp
  have h' : ((W p : ℝ)) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast h
  have hnn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg p
  have hsq : Real.sqrt p ^ 2 = (p : ℝ) := Real.sq_sqrt hnn
  have hs : 0 ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt p := by positivity
  nlinarith [abs_nonneg ((W p : ℝ)), sq_abs ((W p : ℝ)), hsq, Real.sqrt_nonneg (p : ℝ)]

end JacSign
